newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble stable on client buying, T-bill auctions.
newsitem.headline: Rouble stable on client buying, T-bill auctions.

text.p: The rouble was steady on Tuesday and dealers said its decline had been braked by bank client buying and demand for roubles ahead of Wednesday's government bond auctions.

"Banks seemed to have long dollar positions in early trading. They closed them and bought roubles as the central bank raised its dollar rates only two points," Moscow Business World bank dealer Nikolai Zolotaryov said.
He added tomorrow's auctions of Treasury bills and OFZ bonds could be another usual reason for the rouble to have stopped its decline for some time.
On September 11 the central bank is auctioning 7.5 trillion roubles of six-month T-bills and 3.5 trillion roubles of an additional tranche of OFZ interest-bearing bonds.
Another dealer said the rouble had firmed shortly in early trading on bank client orders to sell dollars.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,373-75 per dollar compared with an early 5,377-80 and 5,376-78 late on Monday. Tomorrow roubles were currently the same as late yesterday, 5,377-79 per dollar.
The central bank said it had set 5,341/5,381 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Tuesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 20-30 percent compared with Monday's late 1-5 percent.
